o1.biggest_strength: The revenue math covers the whole segment: a base case, a downside case (-$20.3k a month) and a break-even (the plan loses money if more than about 1 in 3 Team 8+ customers move down). The test and stop rules are built on those numbers, including a Team downgrade arm.
o1.biggest_mistake: The Team comparison is muddled: it says 11 channels on Team cost about $121 when that is the 10.4-channel average. The yearly-billing push is only a side note on the switch email, not a standalone quick win.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the yearly-billing offer a proper second lever with its own estimate, and fix the small Team price inconsistency.

o2.biggest_strength: It is a clean, honest package: bad news first, a per-1,000-switchers table with three churn scenarios, a randomised test with a delayed control, and ready-to-paste invite email, pricing card and public post.
o2.biggest_mistake: The revenue math never sums to a total net figure for the segment. It sets aside the yearly-billing quick win, which the owner would want pushed, and the Team downgrade guard only starts after launch, not in the test.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a segment-level net revenue case with a downside, test the Team downgrade rate before launch, and include a cheap yearly-billing nudge.

reason: Both pick the same flat Agency plan, but Output 1 shows the full net revenue picture, including the downside and the break-even on Team downgrades, and tests that risk up front. Output 2 has slightly better copy, but its math is thinner at the decision level.
